precepts.text: Who was God warning? Solomon. What was Solomon's problem beyond the sin itself? Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. He could not take correction; nobody could tell him anything. From that flowed all his other problems. Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: fear God and keep his commandments. But he should not have had to go through it, with all the wisdom given to him and his father's life before his eyes.
precepts.point: Then will I pluck them up by the roots, and make them to be a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we went into captivity.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Who was the Lord talking to in 2 Chronicles 7? Solomon. “if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked”, and “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes”, then “will I pluck them up by the roots”. So what was Solomon's problem, outside of the sin itself? Solomon tells it on himself: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.”

That was his problem. He couldn't take correction. He didn't want to hear it; nobody could tell him nothing. That's like some brothers here: they can't be told, they don't want to hear it, they get offended. He was an old, foolish king who could no longer be admonished, and from that trickled all the other problems he had.

Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: to fear God and keep his commandments. But he shouldn't have had to go through that. All wisdom was given to him, and he saw his father's life before his eyes. He was concerned with how the world operated and wanted to experience the world, when we are supposed to be unspotted from this world.

So the forsaking that brought the captivity began with a king who could not be admonished. When you keep repeating something to people who can't be told anything, after a while you lose them. That is why we have to be willing to receive correction.

precepts.text: Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.
precepts.point: Then will I pluck them up by the roots, and make them to be a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we went into captivity.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
The Lord warned Solomon, “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments”; to forsake means to abandon, desert or leave something entirely, a breach of duty, to totally turn your back. Proverbs ties forsaking to hating correction: “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.”

When you have forsaken the way, being corrected is grievous to you. You keep having to be told the same thing over and over, and the one who doesn't want to hear it gets pissed off; he doesn't want to hear it no more. That was Solomon, the old and foolish king who would no more be admonished.

And the end of it is death: “he that hateth reproof shall die.” For Israel it meant being plucked up by the roots out of the land and made a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we are in captivity today. We got jammed up because we would not take correction.

precepts.text: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy. Corrected over and over, and after a while the neck hardens, the scriptures have no effect, there is no contriteness, no shame. If the word of God is not moving you to change after ten years, something is disconnected. The word of God changes you; if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” Often reproved means every time the correction comes, he will not accept it. So he gets corrected over and over, and after a while his neck becomes hardened. He becomes stiffnecked. The scriptures don't have that effect on him anymore; there is no contriteness, no shame. You see brothers always getting stood up, and after a while it's, yeah, okay, put me out, I'll be back.

Why does that happen? The word of God is not moving you to change. You can't be the same person you were before; there has to be some type of growth. How do you find yourself doing the same thing you were doing ten years ago? Why, ten years later, does somebody have to motivate you to go do the work? Something is not firing off; something is disconnected.

The word of God is supposed to inspire you to change. The word of God changes you; the word of God can cure you. If you ain't changing, it is one of two things: you are a heathen, or you are a reprobate, and the kingdom ain't for you. So if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.

That is the other side of 2 Chronicles 7:14. The Lord will hear and forgive and heal the land when his people humble themselves and turn from their wicked ways. The one who hardens his neck against reproof is suddenly destroyed, and that without remedy.

precepts.text: He is Father and Redeemer to Israel; other nations were never called by His name.
precepts.point: The Most High controls the rain, the insects, and the pestilence. The people called by His name are Israel, the same people read through these chapters, and healing follows their humbling and turning, not a general love for all nations.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer.” The Most High is Father and Redeemer to Israel, “the tribes of thine inheritance.”

Then the line that settles who “my people, which are called by my name” are: “We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name.” Other nations were never called by his name.

So the promise of 2 Chronicles 7:14 belongs to Israel, the same people read through these chapters. The Most High controls the rain, the locust and the pestilence, and the healing of the land follows Israel’s humbling, praying, seeking his face and turning from their wicked ways. It is not a general love for all nations.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by thy name, and upon Israel, whom thou hast named thy firstborn.”

The people called by his name is Israel, his firstborn. That is who the Most High speaks to when he says, “If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.” The mercy and the healing are promised to Israel, not to all nations.

precepts.text: The same word to David: he shall not fail a man to sit on the throne if his children keep the way.
precepts.point: The promise means every king of Israel would come through David's lineage. The kingdom continues so long as the house keeps the covenant.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

precepts.why:
Solomon had already prayed it back to the Most High: “keep with thy servant David my father that which thou hast promised him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit upon the throne of Israel; yet so that thy children take heed to their way to walk in my law.”

Now the Most High answers with the same word: if Solomon will walk before him as David walked and observe his statutes and judgments, “Then will I stablish the throne of thy kingdom, according as I have covenanted with David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man to be ruler in Israel.”

The promise means every king of Israel would come through David’s lineage. But it carries a condition: the kingdom continues so long as the house keeps the covenant and his children walk in his law.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

precepts.why:
Then will he hear you, and we all need the Lord to hear us. The Day of Atonement just passed: don’t go in bringing up old stuff. That means you didn’t repent to the Lord; you just had a day you fasted.

“For there is no man that sinneth not.” They always ask, do you sin? Yes, I sin; my thoughts are sin, I have wicked thoughts. Solomon already told us there is no man that sinneth not: each and every one of us has sin in us. “And deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives”: that is us, carried away captive.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves”: if we would just sit back and remember what we did wrong, the wickedness we carried out, and remember our Lord, pray to him and confess whatever we are dealing with. “Saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”: we have to say we have sinned. That is how the Lord will have mercy on you, when you confess your sin, your broken laws, the things you are dealing with. And pray: pray three times a day.

“Then hear thou their prayer”: there are stages you have to go through. First acknowledge the wickedness you did, then confess it to the Lord: I’m a wicked, perverse person, I broke your laws and your commandments, I’m guilty, Lord. Then he hears, “and maintain their cause”: help them in what they are going through, Lord, in this flesh, in the body of sin. “And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee”: we all sin and we all need forgiveness. People ask, Cap, how do you maintain? Second by second, not minute by minute, hour by hour or day by day. A thirty-second commercial is long; look at what you could get yourself into in thirty seconds. Fight second by second, to keep your mind clear and sober and on the lookout for the wiles of the devil.

“And give them compassion before them who carried them captive”: compassion upon us right here in America, in Jamaica, in Trinidad, in Mexico, in Puerto Rico, in Santo Domingo, where we were taken captive. If you want the Lord’s compassion where you are, humble yourself and pray for forgiveness. Don’t go back to your folly after we just got a new clean slate on the Day of Atonement; don’t bring up old stuff you never forgave while you want to be forgiven. The Lord is giving us mercy in this wicked and evil place; take it seriously.

points: Host: There is this quotation I love so much: if my people who are called by my name shall humble themselves, pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, then will I hear from heaven, I will forgive their sins and I'm going to heal their land.
Many Christians quote this verse but they don't understand the first line: if my people which are called by my name.

2 Chronicles 7:14 that many Christians quote, they've never understood that we must go back to our name Israel. What they do is interpret that as Baptist, Pentecostal, Jehovah's Witness, and that's wrong. Israel is the name that God put on us, because Jacob's name was changed to Israel.

Shall humble themselves: humble ourselves to God's laws, that's what we got to do. And pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways: that is the part that many of our people don't want to do, turn from our ways.
Then will the Lord hear your prayers, and will forgive their sin and will heal their land. That's the prophecy, but we have to do it in that order.

points: “If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray”: that is what we have to do, humble ourselves and pray for forgiveness. You want the kingdom of heaven? Humble yourself, take the correction and pray to the Lord.

“And seek my face”: how do you seek his face? Start reading your Bible and studying the scriptures for the things you are going through. Don’t sit there with a lying spirit reading something that has nothing to do with what you are going through. If you are a thief, go to the scriptures about stealing: steal no more. If you are an adulterer or a fornicator, go to those scriptures. Whatever you are is in the Bible; deal with those scriptures to build your spirit up, and build yourself up on your most holy faith.
“And turn from their wicked ways”, while you study the things you are dealing with. “Then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.”

points: “Now mine eyes shall be open, and mine ears attent unto the prayer”: when you are sincere, diligent and loyal to the Lord, he is going to hear you, because you will have that godly sorrow. He will know you are sincere in what you are praying for, what you are dealing with and going through, and he will help strengthen you, because he knows you are real and serious about it.
